name: built-in
about: The built-in Defaults Profile. Copy it (ovcd profile > my.profile.json), edit it, and pass it with --profile. All values are SI, except speeds, which are in knots. A 'hard' range refuses an input; a 'soft' range accepts it with a warning. Hard ranges are physical limits, and keep every input inside what the engine can compute; a copy may tighten a hard range but never loosen it. Soft ranges are the catalogue's Vessel Class envelopes with headroom.

length_overall_m.basis: catalogue single-hull classes span 32 to 225.5 m

beam_m.basis: catalogue single-hull classes span 4.7 to 28.8 m

moulded_depth_m.basis: moulded depth is keel to main deck at the side. Left out, it is the depth-to-beam ratio of the Cargo times the beam (see depth_to_beam_ratio); the 41 reference vessels with a published depth span 2.2 to 12.5 m

depth_to_beam_ratio.basis: the default moulded depth is this ratio times the beam, at the midpoint of the range in the reference vessels with a published depth: dry bulk and container 0.22 to 0.44 (inland and pushed), liquid 0.22 to 0.38 (inland and pushed), gas 0.44 to 0.66 (nearly all sea-going). Only dry bulk and gas Cargo exist so far; liquid has no Cargo yet. catalogue/depth_rule.md lists every vessel against the rule

length_to_depth_ratio.basis: length over moulded depth above about 25 is a very slender hull for its depth; the reference vessels with a published depth are below it

formation_abreast.basis: catalogue pushed convoys are at most 4 abreast

formation_in_line.basis: catalogue pushed convoys are at most 5 in line

block_coefficient.basis: calibrated box barges span 0.883 to 0.995; widened down for shaped gas hulls; 0.3 is the squat method's validity floor (hard)

min_freeboard_m.basis: must also be less than the moulded depth (hard)

bow_rake_length_to_depth_ratio.basis: carried over from the original engine: the horizontal length of the bow rake as a multiple of the moulded depth. The bow void is this rake plus the forward separation or end bulkhead space

pushed_stern_void_m.basis: carried over from the original engine: the aft void of a pushed barge, which has no stern block (the crew, battery and propulsion are on the tug). Used for a pushed Formation only

lightship_factor_t_per_m3.basis: calibrated box barges span 0.095 to 0.1223 t/m3 (calibration/factors.yaml)

max_tank_od_m.basis: a design limit of this tool, not an IGC Code rule: a tank is never wider than this, so a wider hull gets more tanks across. Tank length is limited only by length over diameter, at most 7

hold_wing_void_width_m.basis: carried over from the original engine: the empty space at each side of the hold. The hold width is the beam less two of these. The hold must keep a width that is not negative (hard)

hold_double_bottom_m.basis: carried over from the original engine: the height of the inner bottom above the keel. The hold height is the depth less this, plus the coaming; it must not be negative (hard)

hopper_slope_h_per_v.basis: carried over from the original engine: the slope of the hopper side plates, horizontal over vertical. The hopper bottom is never narrower than 1 m

hatch_coaming_height_m.basis: carried over from the original engine: the hatch coaming above the main deck. It adds to the hold height and to the air draft

n_holds.basis: carried over from the original engine: a whole number. It sets the number of transverse bulkheads (holds plus one) in the hopper steel weight

bulk_end_bulkhead_m.basis: carried over from the original engine: the end bulkhead allowance at each end of a dry-bulk hold. It is taken off the cargo zone at the bow and the stern

hold_fill_ratio.basis: carried over from the original engine: the part of the hold volume that cargo fills

inner_bottom_plate_mm.basis: carried over from the original engine: plate thickness in the hopper steel weight

hopper_plate_mm.basis: carried over from the original engine: plate thickness in the hopper steel weight

hold_bulkhead_plate_mm.basis: carried over from the original engine: plate thickness of the wing and transverse bulkheads in the hopper steel weight

hatch_coaming_plate_mm.basis: carried over from the original engine: plate thickness in the hopper steel weight

tanks_in_line.basis: carried over from the original engine: a whole number of tanks along the hull. Fewer tanks are longer; a tank longer than 7 outer diameters fails the length over diameter check, and a tank too short for its heads makes the hull infeasible

tank_support_height_m.basis: carried over from the original engine: the height of the tank saddles above the inner bottom. The double bottom is the bottom clearance less this, and not less than zero

tank_dome_height_m.basis: carried over from the original engine: the dome above the tank top. It raises the air draft

wing_tank_gap_m.basis: carried over from the original engine: the gap between the wing ballast tank and the cargo tank, per side. The wing tank width is the side clearance less this gap, and not less than zero

wing_tank_height_ratio.basis: carried over from the original engine: the wing tank height as a fraction of the cargo tank outer diameter. It sets the wing plate level, and so the moulded volume in the lightship

tank_wall_thickness_mm.basis: carried over from the original engine: a fixed wall thickness for the shell and the heads. The engine does not check it against a pressure vessel rule

max_speed_kn.basis: the speed-power grid starts at 1 kn

air_draft_limit_m.basis: catalogue air drafts span 3.0 to 35.5 m

draught_limit_m.basis: catalogue single-hull draughts span 1.0 to 9 m

channel_depth_m.basis: must also be at least the under-keel clearance (hard)
